## Round 3: review of 2cc5078 (head 57a8749)

Every CodeRabbit thread is answered and resolved. 08b0173 fixes the 12 threads plus the outside-diff rollback finding, and 57a8749 fixes the two findings from the re-review. The changes:

- A refused `scroll.pause` or `scroll.resume` (`scroll_state`) leaves the capture running. It used to end the capture and drop its image. Service test: a second resume.
- A pause after the top was proved and before the first frame clears the proof. Startup has to prove the top again. Stitcher test: before the fix it reported `EndOfContent` with `reachedTop`.
- The way to the top keeps its time budget across a Resume. Only the stats keys the service knows are copied into the view.
- Stop or Cancel inside Resume's quiet period ends the capture; the quiet timer no longer resumes it. An agent pause in that period takes the watch down.
- A watch made while the capture is paused is made hidden.
- The pointer record is one locked snapshot, and the correction decision is published together with it. A pause's record ends at Resume. A motion still in flight when the hand is seen is undone.
- GNOME: put-backs used `NotifyPointerMotion`, which Mutter does not have (46 to 50 offer only `NotifyPointerMotionAbsolute` and `NotifyPointerMotionRelative`). Every GNOME put-back so far went through the absolute fallback. They now use `NotifyPointerMotionRelative`.

k72 (Plasma Wayland), dev build, through the session, VNC and a uinput relative mouse:

- 10 random-start tries on each of 08b0173 and 57a8749: every one stopped by the first click, 1 to 19 ms to pause, 0 capture motions after the pause, 0 corrections.
- Pause and Resume against a capture that was never paused: the same PNG, sha256 `213ac2c7…`, `end_of_content`, 6792 rows.
- Resume twice: the second gets `scroll_state` and the capture runs to its end.
- Stop inside the quiet period: ends `stopped`, never resumed.
- Agent pause inside the quiet period: KWin no longer lists the full-output watch. The build before 57a8749 still had it mapped.
- A pause before the first frame could not be produced on k72, because the first frame arrives about 100 ms after start.

## Round 2: after the acceptance of 4630ddc (head 2cc5078)

The acceptance on GNOME, Hyprland, Budgie and Plasma 6.8.2 ([record](https://github.com/patrick-hudson/put.gd-evidence/tree/a9c4f54a9292d42138e84349581a21b41bcfb31e/records/2026-11-14-scroll-pointer-release-1520-acceptance)) failed. Its helper logs explain each failure. Round 2 evidence: [record](https://github.com/patrick-hudson/put.gd-evidence/tree/ee405a20859dda20019e852e0baf61f8db33cbdd/records/2026-11-14-scroll-pointer-release-1514-round2).

1. **Every capture took 2 to 4 times as long as the nightly, and on Hyprland it hit the 180 s limit** (Plasma 145 steps against 75, Budgie and GNOME 176 against 60, Hyprland 133+ against 64, every one of them one notch). With the pointer resting on the bar below the region, the wheel point sits 48 px above the bottom edge. The step planner kept appended rows 24 px below the wheel point, so no step could be longer than one notch. A pointer that only visits for the wheel step is outside while frames are read, so that margin now applies only to a pointer parked on the page (1b07533). After the fix, k72 captures take 28.4 / 28.3 s against the nightly's 27.9 / 28.1 s, with the same images. On the Omarchy guest, back to back, they take 68.8 / 77.6 / 66.1 s against the nightly's 93.8 / 86.4 / 83.3 s, all `end_of_content`.
   The watch was not the cause. No untouched capture had a false pause. On the software-rendered guest frames come about 12% further apart with it (median 118 against 106 ms), but whole captures took as long with it as without it (A/B on 2cc5078: 69.1 / 87.3 / 71.5 s against 70.2 / 69.2 / 61.0 s). So it stays on Hyprland. `PUTGD_SCROLL_WATCH=0` turns it off for lab comparisons.
2. **The Hyprland try that never paused.** That guest's first frame settled slowly, and the pointer first arrived at its rest 3.2 s in. Detection was armed only then, after the whole gesture. Now any pointer that moves on one of the helper's surfaces while the helper sent nothing in between is the user, from the start of the capture.
3. **The pointer was pulled back once when the hand started during a wheel step.** In order of the commits:
   - The rest on the bar was 3 px from its edge. A hand's first 6 px event left the bar with no motion event, and the leave was taken for the helper's own next visit (GNOME's double pull-backs). It now rests over the state text, at least 14 px inside the bar.
   - The gate closes the moment the hand is seen, before anything is logged; a re-park had gone out 2 ms after.
   - Whether the helper moved the pointer after the hand did is told by the motion event's own time. That is the compositor's monotonic milliseconds, the same clock as the helper's, and it is used only where the two agree within a second. Enters (Qt gives them an earlier event's time) and leaves (no place, no time) only pause; the next motion event decides. A rule that guessed from enters and leaves fired falsely on k72 (b14d79f, 7/10) and is gone.
   - When a pull-back happened, the pointer is put back once by one relative motion of exactly the displacement the helper caused: KWin fake input `pointer_motion`, wlr virtual pointer `motion`, Mutter `NotifyPointerMotion`, none of which is accelerated. Whatever the hand did since is kept, however late its events come (the Omarchy guest delivered them 100 to 200 ms late). The log says `pointer put back by`.
   - On GNOME, which has no watch, a motion on the bar within 12 ms of the pointer's arrival there counts as a pull-back. The put-back can be off by the hand's way during the visit (at most about 60 px at 600 px/s).
   - X11 asks the server before every motion and needs none of this.

The remaining open-loop misses on Hyprland (35469c2: fixed 1, random 2) all share one cause. The helper's move landed within a few ms of the driver's single centering jump, which the driver had computed from a cursor position read just before. So no timed event from before the helper's move exists. With steering by eye: 10 of 10. 2cc5078 only adds the watch switch to 35469c2. GNOME, Budgie and Plasma 6.8.2 were not re-run here: the acceptance worker takes them from run 43608251978.

### Also observed

On the Omarchy guest, 2 of 7 untouched PR-build captures ended `lost_track` at the full height. This is the end proof (`ScrollRun::proveEnd`, unchanged here): the page answered the last step down later than the response wait. All rows were there. The 6 A/B captures on 2cc5078 all ended `end_of_content`.

Still out of scope: on GNOME, a region that fills most of the screen hides the controls and the mouse does not pause (the same on the nightly). That is #1519.

## Round 1 (as first posted)

Part of #1514. Documentation: #1521 (merge after this).

During a scrolling capture the helper moved the pointer into the rectangle for every wheel step and back out, without looking at where the user had it, so a person could not reach Stop. Now the pointer is the user's the moment they touch it.

## What changed

**Where the pointer rests.** Between wheel steps the pointer rests on a surface of the helper's own, outside the rectangle: the bar when it is beside the rectangle (a margin above or below its controls, on the edge nearest the rectangle, so the way to the page stays short for Plasma's shake-cursor effect), else a clear 32 px pad at the old rest spot. Where frames show a painted pointer (Hyprland, labwc) the arrow hangs clear of the rectangle.

**Who moved it, per desktop.** The helper knows where it last put the pointer.
- *All desktops with a rest surface:* the surface reporting the pointer more than 4 px from that point, or the pointer leaving it when no visit into the rectangle was sent, is the user (ordinary Qt enter, leave and move events on the bar's or pad's window).
- *Cinnamon X11 (XTest):* also `XQueryPointer` before every injection: a pointer not where XTest left it is the user. At the end the pointer goes back where the user had it only if the user has not taken it.
- *Plasma, Hyprland, labwc (`KdeFakeInput`, `VirtualPointer`):* nothing can ask where the pointer is, and the first commit missed motion that began while the pointer was in the page for a wheel step (2 of 10 random-start tries on k72). The second commit adds the **watch**: a clear layer surface over the rectangle's output that takes the pointer everywhere except 8 px holes at the wheel points, the bar and the pad. Any pointer event on it is the user. Hidden while paused.
- *GNOME:* no extension change. The resident passes the bar's place from the Shell to the helper (`overlay {visible, rect}`) and the pointer rests on the bar, so motion is seen from the bar's own pointer events. There is no watch and no pad on GNOME (only the Shell places windows), so a motion that starts during a wheel step's ~100 ms visit costs one more move back to the rest before the pause.

**Pause.** On the user's motion the injection gate closes at once, from the event, before the loop looks. `ScrollRun` stops between any two injections, inside a visit and inside a wait (an internal `Interrupted` unwinds to the places that can wait), sends no motion and no wheel step, reads no frame, and keeps its state and the image. The bar says "Paused: you moved the mouse" (or "Paused" for `scroll.pause`) with **Resume**, **Stop** and **Cancel**.

**Resume** (the bar's button once the mouse has been still for 500 ms, or `scroll.resume`) looks at the screen first: the pointer goes back to its rest, and the settled picture is placed against the last stitched frame by pixels alone, never by the wheel's hint. Unmoved or placed: the capture goes on (the next step teaches nothing about px per notch; a pending end is proved again). Not placed after one plain wheel step: that step is scrolled back and the last frame looked for. Otherwise `lost_track` with the exact image and the note "the page moved while the capture was paused and its place could not be found again". A pause before the first frame was stitched goes up to the top again.

**Time limits while paused.** The helper's 180 s run limit leaves pauses out. A pause that lasts 10 minutes ends the capture as Stop with the image kept and a note. The resident has no deadline for a running capture (only for its commands, which answer at once while paused), so nothing there can fail a paused capture as a timeout.

**The bar.** Always says "Move the mouse to pause" while capturing (the way to the top included); one fixed size for every state (sized for the longest texts, Resume hidden outside a pause), so Stop never moves. Stop is enabled on the way to the top. It goes beside the rectangle on its own screen (below, above, left, right, corners) before another screen.

**Agent control.** `scroll.pause` and `scroll.resume` (session methods, `putgd-cli`, MCP `control_scroll_capture` pause/resume); `paused` and `pausedBy: "pointer" | "request"` in `scroll.inspect` and the progress event (its `state` is `paused`).

## Acceptance: 10 tries per row

Second pointer moved from the middle of the screen to Stop at 600 px/s, one event every 10 ms, starting 2 s into a capture of en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linux in Firefox, then a click. **VNC**: the wall VNC server on loopback (absolute positions). **uinput**: a relative mouse from `/dev/uinput`, as a real mouse moves. Full method, raw rows and drivers: [evidence record](https://github.com/patrick-hudson/put.gd-evidence/tree/a8481f83a23c158d28824cd3728974f68e214eef/records/2026-11-14-scroll-pointer-release-1514).

The nightly's VNC clicks land on Stop only because every VNC event re-asserts the position; it still moved the pointer 4 to 8 times. Its "moves" count runs until the session ended.

**Hand checks** (both hosts, PR head): a static page captured unpaused and then paused by the mouse halfway and resumed with the bar gave the same PNG (SHA-256 `213ac2c7…`, 6,792 px, `end_of_content`) on k72 and m74; Stop clicked while the capture scrolled to the top (paused by the pointer first) kept the 720 px viewport with `topReached: false` on both. Only one monitor on k72: the two-monitor placement is the unit test `scrollBarStaysBesideALargeRegion`.

## Tests

- `scroll_stitcher_contract`: pause at 24 points (inside a visit, in a wait, between steps; down and to the top) sends nothing while paused and gives the same image as an unpaused run; a page moved while paused is placed (whole page) or ends `lost_track` with an exact prefix; Stop while paused keeps the image; a pause at its limit ends as Stop.
- `scroll_service_integration`: `paused`/`pausedBy` in inspect, `scroll.pause`/`scroll.resume`, Stop while paused keeps (admitted), Cancel while paused discards (no admission, no files).
- `scroll_capture_x11`: another X client moves the pointer during a real helper capture on Xvfb: paused with `pausedBy: pointer`, no injected event for a second, pointer left there; Resume goes on.
- `bar_placement_contract`: beside a large region before another screen.

All four passed on k72; CI passed on 552cc0d and 4630ddc.

## Hyprland, Budgie (labwc) and GNOME: what an acceptance round must check

- Helper log (`PUTGD_RECORD_DEBUG_LOG`): `scroll: rest on the bar at …` (or `on the pad`), and on Hyprland and labwc `scroll: watch over <output> with holes at …`; never `no rest surface` for a region that leaves room.
- Captures still complete: a fixture and a live page end `end_of_content` with every band exact; the watch must not change frames or block the wheel (no `scroll_no_movement`); on Hyprland and labwc no painted arrow in the image (the rest spot keeps the arrow clear).
- The 10 tries (VNC or the guest's own input and a relative device): paused within tens of ms, 0 helper pointer moves after the first motion, first click stops it; plus 10 with a random start time (motion that begins during a wheel step: caught by the watch, log `pointer at … on the watch`).
- Pause and Resume give the same PNG as an unpaused capture of a static page; Stop on the way to the top keeps the viewport.
- While paused the desktop works: other windows take clicks (the watch is hidden), the bar's Resume, Stop and Cancel work; Resume waits until the mouse is still.
- A region that fills most of the output: the bar beside it; where it cannot be, the pad (log) and moving the mouse still pauses.
- Several outputs (Hyprland): the watch is on the rectangle's output only; the holes line up with the wheel points (version 2 virtual pointer mapping).
- GNOME: `rest on the bar at` with the Shell's position (the resident's `overlay` rect); motion on and off the bar pauses; expected gap: motion that starts during a wheel step's visit gets one move back to the rest first (no watch on GNOME); the Shell still places the bar only below, above or on another monitor.

## Gaps left as they are

- **A region that covers its whole output** has no place outside it: no bar, no rest surface, so moving the mouse does not pause and nothing on screen says so. Stop there is Esc on X11, the `scroll` hotkey or `scroll.stop`. The same on GNOME when the Shell found no spot for the bar. Left for the capture-loop rework, as the issue says.
- **One screen, no room for the bar beside the region** (the bar needs about 630×52 px): the bar is hidden as before and the pointer rests on the pad; moving the mouse pauses the capture, but nothing on screen shows Resume or Stop. `scroll.resume`/`scroll.stop`, the hotkey (Stop) and Esc on X11 still work; a pause ends by itself after 10 minutes, keeping the image.
- **GNOME** as above (one move back during a visit; Shell placement unchanged).

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Pause and resume scroll capture from the on-screen control or capture controls.
  * Moving the pointer during capture pauses scrolling; the capture bar shows the pause reason and lets you resume when ready.
  * The capture bar can appear beside the selected area when there isn’t room above or below.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Paused captures retain their progress and can be stopped or cancelled while preserving the appropriate results.
  * Resuming after scrolling the page while paused helps the capture continue from the updated screen; if tracking is lost, the captured image so far is retained.
